3. The defendant No. 2, Begum Asmatunessa Khatun appeared in the suit and filed an application under order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil procedure for transposition herself as plaintiff from the status of the defendant. However, the Trial Court by an order dated 4.10.2000 allowed the said application. Thereafter, the original defendant Nos. 3-6 filed an application for transposing them as plaintiffs and since there is no conflict between them and the original plaintiffs as they all are admittedly co-sharers in the suit property, their application for transposing them as plaintiffs was allowed by an order dated 18.7.2001 without any objection from either side. The said original defendant Nos. 3-6 after being transposed as plaintiffs on 13.3.2002 filed an application under Order 6 Rule .17 of the Code of Civil Procedure for amendment of the plaint stating that the plaintiff No.1 and defendant No.1 are in exclusive possession of their paternal suit property as described in "Gh" schedule of the plaint which needs to be recovered Prom the possession of the plaintiff No. 1 and defendant No.1 by a decree of recovery of Khass possession from them. On the other hand, on 13.4.2003 the plaintiff No. 1 also filed an application under Order 23 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure to withdraw the suit for filing the same afresh. Ultimately after hearing both the applications the learned Trial Court by the impugned order No. 59 dated 27.5.2003 allowed the application for amendment of the plaint (Annexure-B) and also asked the plaintiff -petitioner No. 1 (A) to show cause why the suit will not be dismissed. After that the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1 (A) without filing any show case filed an application for recording her evidence on commission in support of her application and that application was also rejected by the second impugned order No. 61 dated 1.7.2003 and fixed the next date on 30.7.2003 for P.H. 

 4. Mr. A.Y. Mashihuzzaman, the learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the learned Trial Court committed an error in passing the impugned orders inasmuch as he over looked the material legal aspects that the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 by making prayer for recovery of possession has made out a case of altogether different nature from the case of the plaintiff- petitioners and by virtue of the aforesaid amendment now the interest of the plaintiff-petitioner conflicts with the Interest of the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 and in that view of the matter the plaintiff-petitioners. Petitioners have no other alternative but to file an application for withdrawal of the suit and the learned Trial Court committed further illegality in not allowing the plaintiff-petitioners to withdraw the suit as the predecessor of the petitioners was the original plaintiff in the suit. Mr. A.Y. Mashihuzzaman, further submitted that the prayer for recovery of possession is superfluous and unnecessary inasmuch as every co- sharer is deemed to be in possession of the property and in the event of passing a preliminary decree they will automatically get their shares by evicting other sharers from 1 their possession of the property. 

 7. We have gone-through the petition and the papers annexed therewith and (carefully scrutinized the impugned orders. At the end of the day it appears to us that Mr. A. Y. Mashihuzzaman in one breath admits candidly their the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 are admitted co-sharers of the property and at the same time his grievance is that by making a prayer for recovery of possession they have now made out a case which is in conflict with the interest of the plaintiff petitioners. We failed to understand this submission because he also admits that in the event of preliminary decree the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 will be given the possession of their shares in the suit property by evicting the other co-sharers, namely the plaintiff No. 1 and the defendant No. 1 who are in exclusive possession of the suit property, Therefore, the plaintiff-petitioners are not adversely affected by the amendments brought about in the plaint by the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 Mr. Moshihuzzaman then contends that the plaintiff-petitioner was the original plaintiff and since she wants to withdraw the case the Trial Court most illegally and without jurisdiction disallowed her to withdraw the case, We do not find any substance in this submission as will. The settled legal position is that a suit can be withdrawn with a prayer for re-filing the same on the ground of formal defect but in the instant Case Mr. Mashihuzzaman has failed to lay his hand to any such formal defect rather his grievance is that he is aggrieved by the prayer for recovery of possession but Mashihuzzaman also admits that in any event the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 will get their due shares after the preliminary decree. It appears to us that the application filed by the plaintiff-petitioner under order 23 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure is misconceived and incompetent in the facts and circumstances of the case. In that view of the matter the Trial Court ought to have rejected the said application-but instead he has kept that application in the filed for the time being and asked the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1(A) to show cause why the suit shall not be dismissed. In the facts and circumstances of the case for filing an application under order 23 Rule 1 of the Code without showing any formal defect and for non-compliance with the show cause notice the Trial Court cannot dismiss the suit inasmuch as the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1(A) is no more the sole plaintiff. There are other five plaintiffs. Moreover, it is a partition suit and all the parties stand at par by he or she plaintiff or defendant. If for some reasons or other the plaintiff-petitioner feels aggrieved due to the amendment she can transpose herself as defendant in the suit but that cannot be a ground for allowing her to withdraw from the suit, more so, when all parties are admitted co-sharers of the suit property. In the ultimate analysis it appears to us that the prayer for recovery of possession made by the plaintiff Nos. 3-6 is, in fact, redundant and superfluous and even if it is conceded to that extent the impugned order is defective but that alone cannot be the ground for interference with the impugned order inasmuch as it does not cause error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 8. We have already indicated that the application filed by the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1(A) under Order 23 Rule 1 of the Code is misconceived and incompetent. In that view of the matter that application is hereby rejected. Since the application filed under Order 23 Rule 1 of the Code is rejected no question thus arises for examining her on commission and also no question does arise at all for asking the plaintiff-petitioner No. 1(A) to show cause why the suit shall not be dismissed as that portion of the second impugned order appears to be illegal and without jurisdiction.
